Tan Ah Kow v Lim Logistics Pte Ltd
[2022] SGCA 60
Court of Appeal — Civil Appeal No 12 of 2022
Sundaresh Menon CJ, Andrew Phang JCA, Judith Prakash JCA
Decision Date: 15 November 2022
Employment Law — Wrongful dismissal — Due inquiry
Contract — Contractual terms — Implied terms

1 This appeal concerns the correct approach to claims of wrongful dismissal on the grounds of misconduct under s 14(1) of the Employment Act 1968.

2 In Ong Chee Meng v Rapid Freight Pte Ltd [2015] SGHC 112, the General Division of the High Court held that an employer need not conduct any formal inquiry before dismissing an employee for misconduct, so long as the misconduct is later proved in court. The appellant submits that this cannot stand with the language of s 14(1).

3 We agree. In our judgment, Ong Chee Meng v Rapid Freight Pte Ltd [2015] SGHC 112 was wrongly decided and is overruled. The words “after due inquiry” in s 14(1) impose a mandatory procedural requirement, and a dismissal effected without due inquiry is wrongful notwithstanding that misconduct is subsequently established.

4 We would add that the decision in Chua Beng Huat v Metro Retail Pte Ltd [2018] SGHC 44 is distinguishable, as it concerned termination with notice under the contract rather than summary dismissal under s 14(1).

5 For these reasons, we allow the appeal. The respondent is to pay the appellant the sum assessed of $45,000 and costs fixed at $30,000 inclusive of disbursements.
